description: Beats, tempo, and onsets by Essentia's RhythmExtractor2013 (multifeature) and OnsetRate on 44,100 Hz audio in overlapping chunks, and how far onsets sit from the beat grid; the primary tempo level by onset support, its alternatives, meter, downbeats, and spans of steady tempo and meter, from the beats and its own spectral flux and chroma. Decodes for itself: both algorithms need 44,100 Hz and finer hops than frames has.

beats.description: the tracker's beats moved onto the onsets' time base, each with an onset within beat_align_ms or onsets within beat_gate_seconds on both sides

onsets.description: OnsetRate's onsets, but none in the first edge_onset_ms; 4 to 15 ms before the attack, by its sharpness

tempo.description: 60 over the median beat interval in the window; 0 where none

onset_count.description: onsets in the window between two beats

onset_deviation.description: mean absolute and mean signed distance of those onsets from the subdivided beat grid, the beats aligned to the onsets on them; positive is late

offgrid.description: mean absolute distance as a fraction of a subdivision: about 0.03 on the grid, 0.25 at random, 0.5 at most

chunk_confidence.description: BeatTrackerMultiFeature's confidence of each chunk, 0 to 5.32; 0 for a chunk that keeps no onset; the last chunk may be shorter than the grid's frame

bpm.description: 60 over the median of every beat interval the tracker kept; 0 with fewer than two beats. A tracker that changes level mid-song makes this a level that may never be played: see primary_bpm

confidence.description: the chunks' confidences weighted by the seconds each keeps

pulse.description: the primary level's beats, from the tracker's beats by the chosen relation; value is the beat's place in its bar, 1 the downbeat, or 0 where the bar's downbeat_margin is below downbeat_margin (the place is a guess)

downbeats.description: the pulses that start a bar, only where the bar's downbeat_margin is at least downbeat_margin; value is the bar's length in beats, label its meter (4/4, 3/4, 12/8, ...). On an album of dense music, at the default margin 81% fell on a neural tracker's downbeats, and 96% at a margin of 2; the others about as often one beat off as half a bar off

primary_tempo.description: the primary level's tempo: the relation of the tracker's tempo (1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 2:1) with the most onset support times a preference for tempi near prior_bpm and one for the tracker's own octave (tracker_octaves wide), through a path that changes level only on sustained evidence and starts afresh after a break without beats; a second where the window's beats are too few to lay every level is no evidence for any; 0 where the tracker has no beat. Octaves are mostly the preferences': the support hardly tells them apart

tempo_support.description: the onset support of the levels at 1:2, 2:3, 3:4, 1:1, 4:3, 3:2 and 2:1 of the primary tempo, in that order: the mean accent on each level's pulses at its best phase, as a fraction of the window's 95th-percentile accent; 0 where there is no primary

downbeat_margin.description: how clearly the bar lines are placed at the last pulse at or before each second: over the 4 bars either side, the mean downbeat evidence (the low accent, less half the whole accent, and half each of the beat-synchronous chroma's move at the beat and across a bar, each a robust z-score) at the bars' first beats less the largest at any other beat of the bar; 2 to 4 on a band whose bar lines carry a kick and a chord change, below 1 where another phase fits as well; 0 where there is no pulse

tempo_spans.description: stretches of one tempo level (within 8%) and one meter; value is the tempo in BPM, label the meter

tempo_changes.description: where one span meets the next: label meter when the beat or its fastest subdivision persists (only the grouping changed, such as 4/4 to 12/8), tempo otherwise; value is the new tempo over the old

primary_bpm.description: the tempo level covering the most time in tempo_spans; 0 with none

meter.description: the meter covering the most time in tempo_spans; empty with none. Where a song's bars are not all of one length, 5 beats a bar is preferred to 4 where they repeat about as well
